transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in today. What brings you to see me?

Hi, thank you. Well, I guess what brings me in is this constant restless feeling I've been having. It's like I’m wound just a bit too tight, and I can’t fully settle down. It happens even when I’m supposed to be doing something calm—like sitting through a long planning meeting at work, or even on my own time when I'm painting or trying to do yoga. I just can't seem to settle.
Along with this restless feeling, do you find yourself constantly worrying about many different everyday things?
No, not really. I don't feel like I'm worrying all the time. It's more of a physical feeling, like I just have to move or do something, rather than my mind spinning with worries about everyday stuff.

{"intent": "Determine whether the restlessness has been present since childhood to evaluate for ADHD.", "question": "Has this feeling of restlessness and difficulty settling down been something you've dealt with since

Yes, pretty much as long as I can remember. Even way back in elementary school, I used to get notes sent home to my parents about my behavior. The teachers would say I kept popping out of my seat, or that I was talking over my classmates. I also had this habit of rushing to blurt out an answer before the teacher even finished asking the question. So, yeah, it's definitely not a new feeling for me.
Do you also struggle with paying attention, such as making careless mistakes, getting easily sidetracked, or having trouble organizing tasks?

Yes, I do have some trouble with careless mistakes. Like, over the past couple of years, I’ll think I’ve checked a vendor spreadsheet really carefully. But then our planning coordinator will catch something—like I transposed a SKU, or maybe I completely missed a freight surcharge, or I carried the wrong quantity into the purchase order. So, yeah, that definitely happens even when I feel like I'm paying attention.
